term: per se (essentially) ordered series of causes
definition: A series of essentially dependent causes: a cause exercising derivative causal power causes only insofar as it is sustained by an upstream cause. This does not presuppose a first member. The stone/stick/hand example motivates the intended here-and-now dependence; a historical father/son succession alone does not identify such a link. The primitive Lean relations MovesAsMoved and CausesAsCaused do not encode time or removal of a sustaining cause. Their here-and-now and removal readings remain OPEN and would require an explicit temporal/intervention bridge. NoInfinitePerSeMoverSeriesReading separately ASSUMES accessibility of every being under MovesAsMoved; well-foundedness is not the definition of an essential link. The efficient-cause relation has its own separate premise and is not silently identified with the mover relation.
note: The old source-derived two-Prop InfiniteRegressImpossibleOnlyInPerSeSeriesReading remains unchanged; it transcribes two assertions rather than constraining causal relations. Analyst sibling STMT-PER-SE-HISTORICAL-SERIES-DISTINCTION checks an explicit essential/historical dictionary and a concrete same-member compatibility witness; see docs/causal-regress-and-grim-reapers.md. The witness is not a metaphysical possibility claim.
